base_member_text: [L1357-L1377] (HIGH/unallocated array access) The Fortran-compatible rank-3 and rank-4 point paths read local allocatables r3 and r4 after the sampling phase instead of pointoutputs, but those temporaries are not allocated there.
audit_member_text: [L1357-L1377] (HIGH/unallocated-access) Fortran-compatible rank-3 and rank-4 point output reads local temporaries r3 and r4 on the I/O path even though extracted values were stored in pointoutputs and those temporaries have already been deallocated or were never allocated there.

base_member_text: [L375-L380,L481-L485,L1025-L1029,L1143-L1147,L1319-L1323,L1780-L1784,L1811-L1812] (MED/unchecked mnemonic lookup) Multiple output paths pass chartoindex results directly to indextos or mnemonic indexing without checking for -1, so an invalid configured variable can become an out-of-bounds access rather than a controlled configuration error.
audit_member_text: [L374-L425] (MED/input-validation) Global variable setup passes unchecked mnemonic indices to indextos, and an unsupported type leaves its ID at -1 but still proceeds to attach attributes to that invalid ID.
[L1025-L1109] (MED/input-validation) Point extraction passes unchecked mnemonic indices to indextos and accepts an unchecked owner rank from space_who_has before point-to-point communication.

base_member_text: [L2127-L2131,L2147-L2151,L2167-L2173] (MED/ignored I/O error) Hotstart writers capture OPEN failures in ierr but never test it and proceed to write and close the unit as if the file were valid.
audit_member_text: [L2124-L2131,L2144-L2151,L2164-L2173] (MED/io-error-handling) All hotstart writers capture OPEN iostat but never check it and then perform unguarded writes and close operations; they also omit replacement semantics for existing files.

base_member_text: [L152-L160] (LOW/error-path state) handle_err attempts to close module ncid even when the failing operation may be nf90_create itself, before ncid has necessarily received a valid file identifier.
audit_member_text: [L152-L160] (MED/error-path) NetCDF error handling always attempts to close module variable ncid, even when the failing operation is file creation and ncid may not yet contain a valid handle.

audit_member_text: [L664-L670] (LOW/duplicate-io) pointtypes is written to the same NetCDF variable twice consecutively.

base_member_text: [L1150-L1198] (MED/rank support inconsistency) Integer global variables are declared for ranks 0 through 4 during initialization, but the writer handles only ranks 0, 2, and 3, silently leaving rank-1 or rank-4 variables unwritten.
audit_member_text: [L1149-L1198] (HIGH/missing-rank-support) Integer global variables are defined for ranks 0 through 4 during initialization, but writing omits ranks 1 and 4 and only prints a message, leaving their records unwritten.

base_member_text: [L481-L527] (MED/uninitialized NetCDF variable id) pointsvarids is not initialized, and an unsupported point-variable type merely prints a message before attributes are written through the unassigned ID.
audit_member_text: [L486-L527] (HIGH/unsupported-type) Point initialization creates IDs only for real variables, but the default branch merely prints for other types and then unconditionally uses the uninitialized pointsvarids entry for attributes.

base_member_text: [L1350-L1371] (HIGH/truncated scientific output) Rank-3 and rank-4 NetCDF point output passes only the single first scalar of each sampled array, so all other vertical/class dimensions remain unwritten despite being declared in the variable.

[L1341-L1370] (MED/point-output shape contract) The point writer supplies no count and uses scalar actuals for multidimensional records, leaving its intended mapping between sampled array dimensions and NetCDF dimensions unclear even when the call succeeds.
audit_member_text: [L1350-L1371] (HIGH/partial-write) NetCDF point output for rank-3 and rank-4 variables writes only element (1,1,1) or (1,1,1,1) while the variables were defined with full trailing dimensions, leaving all other components unwritten.

base_member_text: [L1099-L1102] (HIGH/wrong array component) The non-MPI rank-4 point path sizes its third dimension from t%r3 instead of t%r4, which can dereference an unassociated rank-3 component and allocates the wrong shape.
audit_member_text: [L1088-L1102] (HIGH/wrong-rank-component) The non-MPI rank-4 point path allocates its third dimension from t%r3 instead of t%r4, potentially dereferencing an unassociated pointer and producing the wrong shape.

base_member_text: [L1396-L1406] (MED/wrong file unit) The runup-gauge loop writes unit ii+par%npoints but flushes unit i+par%npoints, where i is stale from the preceding point-variable loop.
audit_member_text: [L1402-L1406] (MED/wrong-index) The runup-file loop writes unit indexed by ii but flushes unit indexed by stale variable i, potentially flushing an unrelated or unconnected unit.

base_member_text: [L412-L415,L513-L516,L600-L603,L1689-L1691] (HIGH/MPI-unsafe termination) Initialization and dimension errors on the output-master-only path use STOP rather than the coordinated halt routine, which can terminate one MPI rank while leaving the others blocked.

[L531-L554] (MED/invalid coordinate metadata) Each drifter trajectory variable declares coordinates='pointx pointy' even though those coordinate variables use the unrelated fixed points dimension rather than the drifter trajectory dimensions.

[L1510-L1539] (MED/output side effect) Writing legacy mean minima and maxima mutates the live accumulated arrays by replacing sentinel extremes with -999, so output changes model-owned statistics rather than formatting a copy.

audit_member_text: [L127-L130,L169-L247,L1134-L1136,L1300-L1302,L1554-L1559] (HIGH/uninitialized-state) The NetCDF-only initializer never initializes saved output counters, while ncoutput increments them and uses itd directly as the drifter record index; those counters are initialized only by fortoutput_init.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: The saved counters are initialized only in fortoutput_init:L1759-L1765, which output.F90 does not call for NetCDF-only output. ncoutput increments the undefined itd and uses it directly as the NetCDF drifter record index; tpar counters used for other coordinates do not neutralize that read.

[L481-L517] (HIGH/bounds-before-validation) Point-variable setup reads dimensions(1) and dimensions(2) before verifying rank is at least 2, so a scalar or rank-1 selection accesses dimension metadata out of bounds.

audit_member_text: [L591-L603] (LOW/diagnostic-accuracy) Rank errors while defining mean variables report mnem even though that variable is not assigned in the mean-variable loop and can contain stale text from an earlier loop.

[L790-L802] (HIGH/feature-gating) Point/runup processing is conditioned on npointvar being positive, so a valid runup-only configuration with gauges but no ordinary point variables never writes point time or runup output.
dispositions.rationale: span-refuted: The premise npointvar=0 with initialized runup gauges is neutralized by params.F90:L2259-L2280: readpoints adds xz, yz and zs to pointvars and increments npointvar whenever runup gauges exist. audit_member_text: [L1139,L1305,L1415] (HIGH/time-scaling) Global, point, and mean NetCDF times are always multiplied by morfac, whereas the rest of the module and BMI time API apply that scaling only when morfacopt equals 1.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: The NetCDF global, point and mean writes multiply by max(morfac,1) without testing morfacopt. In this same routine the Fortran point and dims.dat time paths explicitly test morfacopt, so morfacopt=0 with morfac>1 yields inconsistent time scaling.

audit_member_text: [L1843-L1857] (MED/stale-output) Lazily opened global Fortran files omit status='replace', so an existing longer file from a prior run can retain stale trailing records.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: The lazy open uses direct access without replacement and subsequently writes records using NEXTREC. Existing global files are not replaced in fortoutput_init, so overwriting fewer records can leave the previous run's trailing records intact.
